s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, itchy skin lesions with dermoepidermal separation and milia
salient_findings: Multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques on the left shin
Milia and erosions with partially detached epidermis
key_facts: Female patient in her 30s
Symptoms have been present for more than 10 years
Lesions are localized to the left shin
Lesions are itchy
Milia are present in the superficial dermis
Erosions with partially detached epidermis are present
No abnormalities of the mucous membranes, nails, hair, or teeth
No extracutaneous involvement
Histopathologic examination shows dermoepidermal separation
Genetic testing identified a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1

shortlist.label: Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Genetic testing identified a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1, which is a known cause of this disease

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Acquisita
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of itchy, progressive skin lesions with dermoepidermal separation and milia is consistent with this disease

shortlist.label: Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathologic examination showing dermoepidermal separation is consistent with this disease

shortlist.label: Kindler Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of itchy skin lesions with dermoepidermal separation and milia, as well as genetic testing results, make this disease a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Bullous Pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of itchy, progressive skin lesions is consistent with this disease, although histopathologic examination is not typical

shortlist.label: Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of itchy, progressive skin lesions is consistent with this disease, although histopathologic examination is not typical

shortlist.label: Inherited Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Genetic testing results and clinical presentation make this disease a plausible diagnosis, although specific subtype is unclear

shortlist.label: Pemphigus Vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of itchy, progressive skin lesions is consistent with this disease, although histopathologic examination is not typical and other features are not present

raw.rationale: The presence of dermoepidermal separation, milia, and erosions with partially detached epidermis, along with the identification of a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1, supports the diagnosis of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.

rejected.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Acquisita
rejected.why: The long-standing nature of the symptoms and the genetic findings are not typical for an acquired condition.

rejected.label: Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa
rejected.why: The presence of a COL7A1 mutation and the specific histopathologic findings are more consistent with dystrophic than junctional epidermolysis bullosa.

rejected.label: Kindler Syndrome
rejected.why: While Kindler Syndrome involves skin fragility and blistering, the specific genetic and histopathologic findings in this case are more consistent with Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.

rejected.label: Bullous Pemphigoid
rejected.why: The absence of mucous membrane involvement and the specific histopathologic and genetic findings do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and genetic findings do not align with this condition, which typically involves linear IgA deposits at the basement membrane zone.

rejected.label: Inherited Epidermolysis Bullosa
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa; the specific diagnosis of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa is more precise given the genetic and histopathologic findings.

rejected.label: Pemphigus Vulgaris
rejected.why: The clinical presentation, histopathologic findings, and genetic results do not support an autoimmune blistering disease like Pemphigus Vulgaris.
